newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe drafts law to regulate unit trusts.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe drafts law to regulate unit trusts.

text.p: Zimbabwe has drafted a law governing the operations of unit trusts, to be presented to parliament in March, state officials and consultants who drafted it said on Wednesday.
They told a press briefing that the Collective Investment Schemes bill would help regulate unit trusts that have started to mushroom in the southern African country in the last five years.

There are seven registered unit trusts in Zimbabwe, governed in the interim by ad hoc rules, including one that requires them to submit monthly asset and investment registers to the registrar of financial institutions.

Sally Buxton and Mark St Giles, managing director and chairman respectively of Cadogan Financial of Britain, were contracted by Zimbabwe and the International Finance Corporation (IFC) to assist in drafting the bill.
They said a properly regulated unit trust industry would help harness both foreign and domestic investment, and also boost foreign confidence in the country's financial markets.
Under the proposed legislation, any operator of an unregistered unit trust or any collective investment scheme faces a fine of one million Zimbabwe dollars (U.S.$91,000) or 10 years in jail or both.
